_readme: The save point, walked to and used - the other half of GameConfig.save_policy, shown on a
path a player takes rather than only asserted in a suite.
Every leg is held until a WALL or a BODY stops it, so nothing here is a computed number of
tiles: north out of the spawn is stopped by the warden's body, west along that row by the
map's edge, and north up the edge by the chronicler himself. The last one is the point - he
is the wall this walk is aiming at, so the player arrives facing him with no count involved.
It deliberately does NOT touch the pause menu. This game still saves anywhere, so the Save
row is right there - and a session that used it would prove the old path again rather than
the new one. save_and_load.json is the menu's session and is untouched.
The slot is written and then LOADED BACK from the title, because a save nobody reads is a
file, not a save. The reload is what proves the bytes were real.

steps.text: a qa run empties user://qa_saves at boot, so the cursor opens on New game. One press starts the run.
north until the warden's body stops it - she stands one tile up from the spawn
west until the map's edge stops it
north up the edge until the chronicler's own body stops it, which leaves the player facing him
he asks; the first choice is the one that records
the slot list, opened by a conversation. It arrives AFTER the talk has closed, which is what the deferral buys - opened inline, the dialog's own close would take it straight back off.
a write leaves the screen open, so this is still the save point
walk away, so a load has somewhere to come back from
and the proof the file is real: load it from the pause menu and land back on the mark. Rows are Resume, Items, Equipment, Status, Save, Load - five move_downs to Load.
